newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan"s Kyodo news agency says Deng hospitalised.
newsitem.headline: Japan"s Kyodo news agency says Deng hospitalised.

text.p: China"s paramount leader Deng Xiaoping suffered a brain haemorrhage at his Beijing home last Friday and has been taken to hospital, Japan"s Kyodo news agency said on Wednesday.
In a report from Beijing quoting unidentified "Chinese sources", Kyodo said: "Deng was in critical condition for a few days and is still being nursed with great care."

"President Jiang Zemin cut short a trip to coastal Jiangsu Province due to Deng"s condition and immediately convened the Chinese Communist Party"s Political Bureau to discuss Deng"s health and the defection bid via China of a high-ranking North Korean official," Kyodo quoted the sources as saying.
"The party and the government have instructed high-ranking officials to continue work as usual to avoid adverse effects on the country"s economic construction, the sources said.
"Senior-level officials were advised to go ahead with trips outside the capital scheduled for this week, they said."
A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman on Tuesday dismissed reports that Deng, 92, was in critical condition.
"There has been no major change in Comrade Deng Xiaoping"s health. I have nothing new to report," the spokesman told a regular news conference.
But the spokesman failed to reiterate the government"s frequently expressed view that Deng "is healthy for a man of his age".
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun, a Japanese business daily, said in a report on Wednesday quoting diplomatic sources in Beijing that Deng was critically ill after suffering a brain haemorrhage.
